newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Finnish forestries' profits slid in Jan-Aug.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Finnish forestries' profits slid in Jan-Aug.

text.p: Finnish forestry groups UPM-Kymmene and Metsa-Serla on Thursday reported sharply lower January-August profits and were only tentatively optimistic about a turnaround in the pulp and paper business cycle.

UPM-Kymmene Oy, Europe's largest forestry concern, said profit before extraordinary items slid around 41 percent to 2.67 billion markka ($582 million) from 4.54 billion in the year-ago period, on net sales down to 33.82 billion from 35.62 billion.

"Because of the fall in sales prices and under-utilisation of manufacturing capacity, UPM-Kymmene expects profitability during the remainder of the year to be about the same as that for the four months to August," it said in a statement.

Further ahead, it said economic growth was forecast to strengthen gradually in Europe, its main market, which would increase paper consumption. But market pulp prices -- which appear to be strengthening only gently after slumping from peaks last year -- are still difficult to predict.

Metsa-Serla Oy, Finland's third biggest forestry group, reported a collapse in January-August profit and forecast a loss for the last four months of the year, although it said it would make a profit over the full year.
Profit after financial items fell to 254 million markka from 1.29 billion a year earlier, on net sales up at 9.53 billion from 8.64 billion.

"According to present estimates, Metsa-Serla's result after financial items for the last four months of the year is likely to show a loss," it said. "However, the result for the year is expected to show a profit."
"Market pulp prices bottomed out during the spring and a slight upward trend was visible by the end of the summer," Metsa-Serla said. "Prices for fine papers are expected to embark on a modest rise."

"The improvement in product prices has not come in time to have any material effect on results for the final four months," it said, adding that an unspecified one-off cost of around 300 million markka would weigh on full-year earnings.
Both results were slightly above share analysts' forecasts -- for UPM-Kymmene, the median of forecasts was for a 2.48 billion markka profit after financial items in a 2.20 to 2.84 billion range.
For Metsa-Serla, this was for a 236 million markka profit in a 150 million to 441 million range. ($1=4.59 Markka)
